disease_label_per_paper: Hemolytic uremic syndrome with simultaneous Shiga toxin producing Escherichia coli and complement abnormalities
presentation_summary: 10-year-old boy developed non-bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain, then lethargy, emesis, confusion, jaundice, bruising, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, and profound renal failure.
Initial labs showed hemoglobin 4.5 g/dL, platelets 86 K/uL, sodium 124, potassium 6.0, bicarbonate 13, BUN 329 mg/dL, creatinine 21.8 mg/dL, LDH 4067 IU/L, and normal PTT.

He required platelet and packed red blood cell transfusions, hemodialysis, renal biopsy, intubation/extubation support, and therapeutic plasma exchange because of concern for atypical/complement-amplified HUS.
Stool culture was negative for E. coli O157:H7, but stool Shiga-like toxin enzyme immunoassay later returned positive; ADAMTS13 was normal and renal biopsy showed TMA.
Genetic testing later found complement factor H Gln950His and homozygous CFHR1/CFHR3 deletion; he recovered with normal renal function at 1 year.
